rationale: A wins because it gives the founder four real lanes, not four costumes for the same launch. "The finance team that stopped wiring reimbursements across borders" is the most useful angle in either set because it moves from Brex's announcement to a reporter-usable buyer story, with proof requirements that would actually make or break the pitch. B is competent, but "category-creation" and "the category is consolidating from per-region tools into a single global stack" inflate a product launch into a market thesis the update did not prove. That is how you get a polite pass from a reporter who has seen this movie before.
gaps_in_A: "The finance team that stopped wiring reimbursements across borders" assumes wires were the prior reimbursement method. It is a good customer-story lane, but the headline gets ahead of the supplied facts.

"How Brex built card issuing and local-currency reimbursement in 50 countries" slightly overstates what is known. The update says Brex is launching the capability, not that Brex built direct issuing infrastructure itself.

"Enterprise customers pushed Brex, the startup card company, to go global" leans on a reputation claim. The facts say many customers are venture-backed startups; they do not say Brex is still chiefly understood as a startup card company.
The set is strong, but every live angle still needs one hard asset before pitching: country list, named customer, competitor comparison, or enterprise-request data.
gaps_in_B: "The 50-country launch is live today" is too confident. The update says current time and says Brex is launching; A was right to say confirm whether it is live now or announced for later.
"category-creation" is puffed-up positioning. Nothing in the update proves Brex is creating a category, only expanding product availability across markets.
"the category is consolidating from per-region tools into a single global stack" invents a market trend from one company-supplied launch. That needs outside evidence or it belongs in the trash.
B misses a clean standalone customer-story angle. It asks for a named finance-ops user as proof, but never turns that buyer's pain into its own pitchable lane.
